Find the arc length $L$ of the polar curve $r=6{e}^{\theta }$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{8}$ (shown in blue in the diagram above). Do not round the answer.

$L=6\sqrt{2}($
{{field-1}} $)$
worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=6{e}^{\theta },$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=6{e}^{\theta }.
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /8}\sqrt{{(6{e}^{\theta })}^{2}+{(6{e}^{\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /8}\sqrt{36{e}^{2\theta }+36{e}^{2\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /8}\sqrt{72{e}^{2\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =6\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /8}{e}^{\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =6\sqrt{2}\,{e}^{\theta }{|}_{0}^{\pi /8} \\  & =6\sqrt{2}({e}^{\pi /8}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =6\sqrt{2}({e}^{\pi /8}-1).\end{aligned}
$$
